column7: DeleteProjectIfEmpty counted the project's live secrets BEFORE taking the project row lock -- one call frame too late, since deleteProjectCascade already locked correctly before its own sweep but this function's own count ran before deleteProjectCascade was ever reached. This let CreateSecret's write-then-FOR-SHARE protocol (lockLiveParent) interleave with DeleteProjectIfEmpty: CreateSecret inserts and takes FOR SHARE uncontended (the count hadn't locked yet); DeleteProjectIfEmpty counts and sees 0 (the insert is still uncommitted, invisible under READ COMMITTED); DeleteProjectIfEmpty proceeds into the cascade, which blocks on the project row lock CreateSecret now holds; CreateSecret commits, reporting success; the cascade's lock then acquires and its FRESH secret sweep finds and soft-deletes the just-created secret as part of deleting the project. A non-force delete removed a project that, at the moment its caller was told "created", held a live secret. Fixed by extracting the project row-lock (lockProjectRowForCascade, Postgres-only) and calling it at the TOP of DeleteProjectIfEmpty's transaction, before the count, not only inside deleteProjectCascade -- forcing CreateSecret's own FOR SHARE re-check to wait for DeleteProjectIfEmpty's transaction regardless of which one started first. Proving test forces the exact interleaving via two independent Postgres connections synchronized with channels (not a blind scheduler-dependent race): RED (fix reverted) -- blockingSecretCount==0 and the project row is gone entirely, secret destroyed; GREEN (fix applied) -- blockingSecretCount==1, project survives, secret survives live and unreviewed.
